clue.text: Providing evidence for and against company a politician joined

parts.note: con means against, as in pros and cons
a firm is a company
a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party

explanation.surface: A coalition story: a firm and a Tory politician join forces, with the evidence cutting both ways.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for and against' looks like one phrase, but 'for' ends the definition and 'against' gives CON.
explanation.definitionFit: Confirmatory evidence is evidence that supports or corroborates a claim, so the adjective means providing evidence for it.

clue.text: Kind of humour mostly about right to make one laugh

indicators.note: about means the shortened word goes round the next piece
mostly means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: choler, or yellow bile, was one of the four bodily humours of old medicine
Rt is the standard abbreviation for right, as in Rt Hon

explanation.surface: A dry note that a certain style of comedy, roughly right, will get a laugh.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Humour' suggests comedy, but here it is one of the four bodily fluids of medieval medicine; 'mostly' trims its last letter and 'about' signals the wrap.
explanation.definitionFit: A chortle is a single gleeful chuckle, so it is one laugh in noun form.

clue.text: Linked stations in US city disheartened over time

indicators.note: over here means the shortened city name spreads over, or encloses, the next piece
disheartened means the middle letter of the city is taken away

parts.note: New York is the largest city in the US

explanation.surface: Broadcast stations in New York feel downcast as the years go by.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disheartened' removes Y, the middle letter of NEWYORK, leaving NEWORK; 'over' places it round T.
explanation.definitionFit: A network is a chain of interconnected broadcasting stations or railway stations, so linked stations form one.

clue.text: Units invading one Asian country or another

indicators.note: invading means one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: India is a country in Asia
ones are units, the single digits

explanation.surface: Military units invade one Asian country after another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'or another' looks like part of the surface phrase, but 'another' alone is the definition: a second Asian country.
explanation.definitionFit: Indonesia is a second Asian nation besides India, so it is the other country the clue asks for.

clue.text: As foolish person at university, do emergency study

parts.note: a mug is a gullible or foolish person in British slang
up means in residence at university, especially Oxford or Cambridge

explanation.surface: A dim student at college crams frantically before an exam.
explanation.walkthrough: In British usage you are 'up' at university while in residence there.
explanation.definitionFit: To mug up is British slang for cramming a subject quickly, as before an exam.

clue.text: From latest info I learn what can protect food

indicators.note: from means the letters are taken out of the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A reader picks up a kitchen tip from the latest news.
explanation.definitionFit: Tinfoil, or aluminium foil, is the wrapping used to cover and preserve food.

clue.text: What's left by king, say, in other words

indicators.note: by means next to, so the two pieces stand side by side

parts.note: R stands for king, from the Latin rex
an estate is what a person leaves behind at death

explanation.surface: A king's legacy is described again, in plainer words.
explanation.walkthrough: 'What's left' tempts you to REST, but it is ESTATE, a dead person's property; R goes beside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To restate something is to say it again, in other words, so the phrase is a direct synonym.

clue.text: Kind of suit not customized for officer

parts.note: in bridge, spades and hearts are the major suits
general means not tailored to anyone in particular

explanation.surface: An officer's suit was off the peg, not made to measure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suit' suggests clothing, but it is the card-game sense: in bridge, hearts and spades are majors.
explanation.definitionFit: A major general is a senior army officer, ranking above a brigadier.

clue.text: Like issue raised by others and taken up

definitions.meaning: issue means children; a child brought up by other parents is ...
an idea or cause that is taken up has been embraced

explanation.definitionFit: Adopted describes a child raised by non-birth parents and also a proposal accepted or taken up.

clue.text: Seeing changes to second or first book

indicators.note: changes means the letters are rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone sees a second or first book of the Bible being altered.
explanation.walkthrough: SEEING with S added, rearranged by 'changes', makes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Genesis is the opening book of the Bible, so it is the first book.

clue.text: Exhausted old couple in vessel

parts.note: an urn is a vessel
a couple is two

explanation.surface: A worn-out elderly pair rest in a pot.
explanation.definitionFit: Outworn means worn out, used up or exhausted, as of a notion or garment.

clue.text: How could resort make Capri so unromantic?

indicators.note: resort is read as re-sort, so the letters are sorted again

explanation.surface: A traveller wonders how a holiday resort could make Capri seem dull.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resort' poses as a holiday spot but signals re-sorting the letters of CAPRI SO.
explanation.definitionFit: Prosaic means dull, matter-of-fact and lacking poetry, the opposite of romantic.

clue.text: Run into nerdy enthusiast producing language I can't understand?

indicators.note: into means the first piece is put inside the second

parts.note: a geek is an obsessive, nerdy enthusiast
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: Bumping into a nerd results in jargon nobody can follow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It's all Greek to me' is the idiom for something incomprehensible, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Greek is used idiomatically for any speech or writing that is completely unintelligible to the listener.

clue.text: Junior officer on warship has to change course

parts.note: a sub, or submarine, is a warship
to alter is to change
N, north, is a compass course or heading

explanation.surface: A junior officer aboard a warship has to alter its heading.
explanation.walkthrough: 'change course' reads as one phrase, but it splits: ALTER for change and N, north, as a course.
explanation.definitionFit: A subaltern is a British army officer below the rank of captain, a junior commissioned officer.

clue.text: British studied fishing equipment in poor condition

parts.note: read means studied, as in read history at university
a line is used for fishing

explanation.surface: A British student who read up on fishing tackle ends up hard up.
explanation.walkthrough: In British usage you 'read' a subject at university, meaning you studied it.
explanation.definitionFit: Living on the breadline means being at subsistence level, a state of poverty.

clue.text: Metal panel cut and arranged it's for handle at entrance

indicators.note: arranged means the letters are put into a new order
cut means the word loses its last letter

explanation.surface: A metal panel is trimmed and fitted by a door.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' trims PANEL to PANE; METAL plus PANE, 'arranged', make the answer. 'handle' is slang for a name, not a door handle.
explanation.definitionFit: A nameplate bears a person's name, slang a handle, and is fixed by a front door.

clue.text: Conductor, as, in parts, employed in underground system

indicators.note: employed in means the letters are put to work inside the next piece
in parts means the two letters go in separately rather than together

parts.note: a metro is an underground railway system
the word as is used as it stands, split into its two letters
the word as is used as it stands, split into its two letters

explanation.surface: An orchestral conductor, doing bit parts, works on the Tube.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as, in parts' tells you A and S go into METRO separately: A after M, S after E.
explanation.definitionFit: A maestro is a distinguished conductor or teacher of music.

clue.text: Code of a sort favouring monarch before PM

parts.note: pro means in favour of
GR, Georgius Rex, is King George's royal cipher
AM marks hours before noon, the half of the day ahead of PM

explanation.surface: A royalist wants the king to take precedence over the Prime Minister.
explanation.walkthrough: 'PM' looks like the Prime Minister, but it is post meridiem, so before it comes AM.
explanation.definitionFit: A program, in the American spelling used for computing, is a set of coded instructions.

clue.text: It's put on bow of ship, initially, one in the navy

indicators.note: in means these letters are placed inside the next piece

parts.note: RN stands for Royal Navy

indicators.note: initially means the first letters of the two words before it

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Something is fitted to a ship's bow by a sailor in the navy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bow' suggests the front of a ship, but the definition means a violin bow.
explanation.definitionFit: Rosin is the resin rubbed on a string player's bow to make it grip the strings.

clue.text: No problem for a show-jumper

definitions.meaning: a no is a turning down of a request
a horse that stops short of a fence and will not jump commits a fault in show-jumping

explanation.definitionFit: A refusal is a no, and in show-jumping a refusal is the horse balking at an obstacle.

clue.text: Kind of indirect tax that's the last, resort

indicators.note: resort is read as re-sort, so the letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A grumble that a hidden levy is the final resort of a government.
explanation.walkthrough: 'last resort' is a familiar phrase, but the comma splits it: 'resort' rearranges THE LAST.
explanation.definitionFit: A stealth tax is one levied indirectly so taxpayers barely notice it.

clue.text: Quickly pronounce dance cancelled

parts.note: a reel is a lively Scottish dance
an event that is off has been cancelled

explanation.surface: Someone announces in a hurry that the dance is off.
explanation.definitionFit: To reel off is to recite a list rapidly and fluently.

clue.text: Half-heartedly attacked criminal

indicators.note: half-heartedly means one of the two middle letters at the heart is dropped

parts.note: fell on means attacked

explanation.surface: A criminal made a feeble assault.
explanation.walkthrough: FELLON's heart is LL; 'Half-heartedly' drops one L.
explanation.definitionFit: A felon is a person who has committed a serious crime.

clue.text: Change course to go to the other side, crossing line

indicators.note: crossing means the first piece goes across, or around, the other

parts.note: to defect is to desert to the enemy side

explanation.surface: A turncoat crosses a border line to join the enemy.
explanation.definitionFit: To deflect is to turn something aside from its course, or to swerve.

clue.text: Lacking imagination, a character fault?

definitions.meaning: taking words at face value, without imagination
in printing, a typo in a single letter, or character, is called this

explanation.definitionFit: Literal means matter-of-fact, and in printing a literal is a misprinted letter.

clue.text: Man, for one, is so narrow-minded

definitions.meaning: the Isle of Man is an island, so it is island-like

explanation.definitionFit: Insular means relating to an island and also narrow or inward-looking in outlook.

clue.text: Break the law on public land in Australia, say

indicators.note: on means the second piece comes after the first

parts.note: a common is open land for public use

indicators.note: break means the letters of the following words are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone flouts the law on a village green in Australia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Break' scrambles THE LAW, giving the second piece; it follows the land.
explanation.definitionFit: Australia is one example of a commonwealth, a federation of states.
